 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. JOHANNESBURG, South Africa (AP) — Towhid Hridoy scored 137 runs off 227 balls as Bangladesh fought back on day one of the first cricket test against host South Africa to reach 327-6 at stumps on Sunday.
 Hridoy hit a second century in only his seventh innings in four tests, scoring 14 fours and a six, as he added 206 runs for the sixth wicket with Litton Das at the Wanderers.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Hridoy was out off the last ball of the day, trapped lbw by a low full toss from Marco Jansen in the 84th over, with the review staying in South Africa's favor.
 Das finished unbeaten on 92 off 138 balls, with 12 fours, as the duo undid South Africa pacer Kagiso Rabada's 3-16 in a fiery six-over spell after Bangladesh had won the toss and opted to bat. Rabada finished the day with 5-51 off 17 overs.
 Bangladesh went to lunch at 91-3 in 26 overs.
 Hridoy and Tanzid Hasan added 99 off 152 balls to revive the innings from 22-3 in 8.5 overs.
 Rabada strikes again
 Rabada struck early in the second session as well when Hasan was unlucky to get an inside edge onto the stumps and was bowled in the 35th over for 67 off 108 balls.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Veteran batter Mushfiqur Rahum was out for a golden duck – caught at third slip – as Bangladesh slipped to 121-5 in 34.2 overs. It was Rabada's 18th five-wicket haul in tests, even as Hridoy began rebuilding the innings again.
 Big and bigger
 This time Hridoy put on an even bigger partnership with Das on either side of tea. Before the break, Hridoy reached 50 off 99 balls, while the duo added 50 off 79 balls. Bangladesh was 184-5 at tea.
 It was almost a wicket-less final session. Hridoy and Das' 100-stand came off 140 balls with another 50 added off further 89 balls.
 Hridoy, who scored 224 against West Indies at Sylhet in his previous test , reached 100 off 194 balls deep into the session. Das got to 50 off 71 balls.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bangladesh crossed 300 in the 78th over.
 The second new ball was duly taken, and Jansen finally delivered the breakthrough to dismiss Hridoy leg before.
 Morning blues
 In the morning, Rabada wreaked havoc with the new ball. Debutant Mahfijul Islam was caught first ball, edging a wide delivery to third slip as Jansen made no mistake.
 Rabada made it two wickets in his eight balls as Mominul Haque was caught behind for a seven-ball duck.
 Skipper Najmul Shanto scored 12 runs but was undone by a sharp inswinger from Rabada, leaving the top-order in tatters.
 The early dismissals brought Hasan and Hridoy together, and they batted out the remainder of the session.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement South Africa took the No. 1 ranking after its recent series win at home against Australia but currently sits second in the World Test Championship table , with New Zealand first. The top two sides will contest the final in June 2027.
 Bangladesh is fifth, after losing 1-0 at home to the West Indies.
